segments.t: What changed in the current release. The version this guide was built for is shown in the footer.

KTPH006Logfile ManagerKTPH007 — KTPH008Tools → Logfile Manager…KTPH009 (KTPH010KTPH000KTPH011+KTPH012KTPH001KTPH013+KTPH014KTPH002KTPH015, KTPH016KTPH003KTPH017+KTPH018KTPH004KTPH019+KTPH020KTPH005KTPH021 on macOS) finds terminal logs in default, connection-specific, previously used and manually added folders. Filter by name, time range, format or compression; inspect file sizes and retention dates; export compressed copies or delete selected files after confirmation. Live logs are protected from deletion. See KTPH022Logfile ManagerKTPH023.

KTPH000Log viewerKTPH001 — open large or compressed logs without loading the whole file into the viewer, search, jump to a line, copy selected lines and highlight keywords, links and paths. JSON and XML logs have a formatted view with a raw-view toggle. See KTPH002Viewing a logKTPH003.

KTPH000Context and badgesKTPH001 — log entries can include the SSH username and the full working directory or a path relative to the first reported directory, subject to enterprise policy. The manager displays connection names and stable aliases for IP-only names, supports searchable custom badges, and offers a KTPH002HoldKTPH003 badge that prevents automatic and manual deletion. See KTPH004Terminal loggingKTPH005 and KTPH006Logfile ManagerKTPH007.

KTPH000Protected exportsKTPH001 — export whole logs or selected lines, optionally trim them to a time range and convert between JSON, XML and plain text. Archives can use AES-256 password encryption and additional GPG encryption. See KTPH002Exporting logsKTPH003.
KTPH000Valid XML after policy replacementsKTPH001 — terminal XML logs remain parseable when an enterprise replacement rule inserts characters XML cannot represent.

KTPH000Customizable icon toolbarKTPH001 — add, remove, rearrange and preview terminal, tool and settings buttons, with a separate row for saved servers and groups. Visibility and layout are shared across windows; icon size is adjustable from 16 to 64 px. The Tools group includes the Logfile Manager, and existing layouts gain its button once while preserving their other buttons and order. The in-window menu bar starts visible. See KTPH002Customizing the icon toolbarKTPH003.

KTPH000Docked panels keep their widthKTPH001 — the AI agent panel, Coding Agents, Live Journal and local file browser retain their selected width beside wide terminals and shrink proportionally when the window has insufficient space.

KTPH000More coding agentsKTPH001 — local shell tabs now also recognise MiniMax Code, Qwen Code, OpenCode, Cursor Agent, Aider, Goose, Crush, Continue, Superagent's Grok CLI, xAI's Grok Build, GitHub Copilot CLI, Jules, Amp and Kiro CLI. Amp and Kiro CLI rules are based on the programs' own texts and remain unverified against live sessions. See KTPH002What it detectsKTPH003.

KTPH000Sidebar and quick answersKTPH001 — the Coding Agents sidebar automatically appears on detection and hides when no agents remain; its selected side is remembered, automatic visibility can be disabled, and KTPH002ExplainKTPH003 details collapse after 60 seconds. KTPH004YESKTPH005 and KTPH006NOKTPH007 send the complete uppercase word followed by Enter, so one click submits the answer. See KTPH008Coding agentsKTPH009.

KTPH000Profile editor in sectionsKTPH001 — the KTPH002ProfilesKTPH003 tab keeps the profile name and KTPH004Use as default profileKTPH005 at the top and groups the fields into KTPH006ConnectionKTPH007, KTPH008Model KTPH022 capabilitiesKTPH009, KTPH010Limits KTPH023 timeoutsKTPH011 and KTPH012Budget KTPH024 usageKTPH013. Only the rows of the selected connection mode are shown, the request timeout that applies to every profile heads the Limits KTPH025 timeouts section, and KTPH014Test AI ConnectionKTPH015, KTPH016DeleteKTPH017 and KTPH018SaveKTPH019 sit under the editor. See KTPH020AI ManagerKTPH021.

KTPH000Local AI in sectionsKTPH001 — the KTPH002Local AIKTPH003 tab splits into KTPH004Profile rolesKTPH005, KTPH006Local runtimeKTPH007 and KTPH008Hugging FaceKTPH009. See KTPH010Text, coding, translation, and embedding rolesKTPH011.

KTPH000Profile setup wizardKTPH001 — a sidebar shows the stages and the choices already made, a KTPH002Quick startKTPH003 finds LM Studio, Ollama (on this computer, on the hosts you enter under KTPH004Other computers on the networkKTPH005, and on the hosts of existing profiles) and installed command-line tools and offers one-click profiles, connection types and providers are cards, reasoning sits under KTPH006AdvancedKTPH007, and the last step runs the test by itself and shows a summary with KTPH008ChangeKTPH009 links. See KTPH010AI Profile Setup WizardKTPH011.

KTPH000Messaging settingsKTPH001 — desktop notification choices now have a dedicated KTPH002MessagingKTPH003 settings page, including a separate switch for coding-agent messages. Saving applies the choices to open sessions. See KTPH004Messaging settingsKTPH005.

KTPH000Notification clicks return to the paneKTPH001 — clicking a desktop notification selects its window, tab and terminal pane. The Flatpak sandbox permits the desktop notification service, and macOS development runs build a native notification helper. The enterprise policy can disable desktop notifications for every feature. See KTPH002Clicking a notificationKTPH003.

KTPH001Import and update external AI skillsKTPH002 — the AI Skills manager imports KTPH000 files from GitHub, SkillsMP and HTTP(S) providers. Provider tokens and passwords are encrypted with the master password, and source updates are previewed as a side-by-side diff. Imported skills start deactivated; only the skill text is imported, with a 256 KiB limit and HTTPS required except for loopback addresses. See KTPH003External skillsKTPH004.

KTPH000Job dependenciesKTPH001 — a job can depend on other jobs and either keep its own schedule but only run when every predecessor's last run succeeded (KTPH002ConditionKTPH003), or start automatically once all predecessors have succeeded (KTPH004ChainKTPH005), optionally only counting recent successes. Cycles are refused, the job list shows a KTPH006Depends onKTPH007 column, and deleting a job that others depend on warns first. KTPH008Run with successorsKTPH009 runs a job and everything below it in dependency order, and KTPH010Disable chainKTPH011 switches a job and all its dependents off or on at once. See KTPH012Job DependenciesKTPH013.

KTPH000Dependency diagramKTPH001 — draws the job dependencies as a Mermaid flowchart colored by each job's last result, vertical or horizontal, in light or dark mode, with SVG/PNG export. See KTPH002Dependency DiagramKTPH003.

KTPH000Log export controls stay visibleKTPH001 — the options dialog is resizable and scrollable, with an explicit KTPH002Export…KTPH003 button that opens the save dialog for one log or a line selection, or a folder chooser for several logs. Export and Cancel stay visible even in a short window. See KTPH004Logfile ManagerKTPH005.

KTPH000Snippet analysis progress stays usableKTPH001 — the checklist remains visible in short panels and after a run finishes, and progress content no longer intercepts clicks on the dialog's KTPH002CloseKTPH003 button. See KTPH004Applying improvementsKTPH005.

KTPH000Complete log translationsKTPH001 — added the missing log context, badge and export labels in Spanish, French, Croatian, Italian, Dutch and Portuguese. The build checks each locale for missing keys and reports their names.

KTPH000Refreshed guide and dependenciesKTPH001 — reconciled the manual with the implemented features, refreshed screenshots, improved dark-theme tree tables, and updated build, documentation and compression dependencies.

Only the current release is listed here, so the guide stays short in every language it is translated into. Every version is on the KTPH002GitHub releases pageKTPH003; the curated notes for earlier versions are kept in the repository, in KTPH000 and KTPH001.
